observations: Two roughly square eye zones sit in the upper half, each built from tight spiral loops with a crosshair of straight lines at the center—the left on a darker local ground, the right on yellow.
A wide mouth shape in the lower half is outlined in thick red loops enclosing white space, with dense black hatching filling the interior and continuing below the chin line.
Broad cyan lines cut across the composition at sharp angles—one near-horizontal band through the mid-section, one diagonal exiting the lower right—against a deep burgundy background.
reading: The face is assembled from competing systems: spirals that pull inward at the eyes, a mouth that opens outward in red arcs, and cyan lines that cut across both without belonging to either. The burgundy field holds the whole thing together. What reads as intensity comes less from any single mark than from the collision of these three separate logics occupying the same space at once.
contextAngle: Within the owned subset of the nifty-faces title family, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nifty faces #18 and nnxyz nifty faces #20; title order and recorded creation order align here. The burgundy ground is distinct from the warm brown of #18 and the white field of #20.

connections.reason: Both works use a blocky face structure with spiral-and-crosshair eye zones, but #18 keeps its spirals open and orange against a warm brown ground, while #19 tightens them into purple-yellow targets against burgundy, sharpening the contrast between the two approaches.

lookingQuestion: The two eye zones share the same spiral-and-crosshair structure but sit on different colored grounds—what does that difference in local color do to how you read each eye relative to the other?
ambiguities: The collector relates this work to scrimshaw through visual qualities (layered line density, light marks on dark ground); this is the collector's stated perspective and is not attributed to the artist.

nnxyz nifty faces #20 and nnxyz nifty faces #9 were inspected but offer no stronger formal connection than #18: #20 shifts to a tilted figure on white with a decorative border, and #9 uses a looser, more diffuse line structure across a lighter field—neither contrast is as specific as the eye-zone comparison with #18.
